correctness.rationale: The norm-decaying H^p semigroup from arXiv:2609.15911v1 gives exact convergent Laplace formulas for all powers. The odd moments of an annihilator of even powers vanish, so an analytic sine transform and Fourier uniqueness force its representing H^q function to vanish. Continuous coefficient duals from gamma products, valid for every p>0, give a common eigenspace of dimension at least ceil(m/2) for the dual of every mth power with m>=3. Polynomial Vandermonde independence and the cyclic C squared upper bound give exact even-power multiplicity. The proof explicitly treats p<1 through coefficient estimates and density, not invalid quasi-Banach Hahn–Banach.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source proves one-step cyclicity and provides the semigroup, but not cyclicity of powers. Direct full-text comparison with that article and the related Lp paper, historical claim comparison, and record searches found no covering power classification. The new sine-transform argument and colliding eigenfunctional construction yield the H^p all-power dichotomy and exact even-power multiplicity. Search noncoverage cannot establish absolute priority; the Kriete–Trutt Hilbert-space model and unindexed equivalent formulations remain risks.

value.rationale: The 2026 theorem establishes cyclicity of the classical C on all Hardy spaces but leaves a natural stability question under positive powers. The new classification exhibits an exact threshold after squaring, independent of p including nonlocally convex H^p, plus a sharp linear growth of generating-vector multiplicity for every even power. These are structural infinite-dimensional properties, not parameter renamings or minor numerical gains.
